rows.text: USSR Law No. 1861-I of 26 December 1990, adopted by the Congress of People's Deputies, renames Chapter 16 of the Constitution 'Кабінет Міністрів СРСР' (item 19) and rewrites Articles 128-136 (items 20-28): new Article 128 makes the Cabinet of Ministers the executive and administrative body of the USSR, subordinate to the President; new Article 129 composes it of the Prime Minister ('Прем'єр-міністр'), his deputies and USSR ministers, its structure set by the Supreme Soviet on the President's proposal; Article 134 is deleted; new Article 136 leaves the Cabinet's competence and procedure to a USSR law. Items 2, 4, 10, 11 and 29 substitute the Cabinet of Ministers for the 'Government of the USSR' in Article 77 and for the Council of Ministers in Articles 96, 122, 124 and 140. Signed 'Президент Союзу Радянських Соціалістичних Республік М.ГОРБАЧОВ', Moscow, Kremlin, 26 December 1990, No. 1861-I.
rows.locator: Items 2, 4, 10, 11, 19-21, 26, 28 and 29; signature and date block

rows.role_title: Chairman of the USSR Supreme Soviet
rows.text: Item 17 renumbers Article 127-10 as 127-7 and replaces 'до Голови Верховної Ради СРСР' and 'до Голови Ради Міністрів СРСР' with 'до Віце-президента СРСР' and 'до Голови Верховної Ради СРСР' respectively, so that the article names the Vice-President and then the Chairman of the Supreme Soviet where it named the Chairman of the Supreme Soviet and then the Chairman of the Council of Ministers. Item 18 adds Chapter 15-2 'Рада Федерації', whose new Article 127-10 provides that the Chairman of the Supreme Soviet may take part in the sittings of the Federation Council.
